name: Call of Duty®: Black Ops III

Optimal.Notes: The 40 Hz refresh + 40 fps cap is the sweet spot for this hardware class — smoother than 30 fps with better battery than 60 fps. Medium textures and shadows look noticeably better than Low with only a modest power increase; FSR at 1024×640 keeps the image sharp on the 1280×800 panel.

profiles.Summary: Call of Duty: Black Ops III runs on the Steam Deck via Proton (Gold tier) with generally playable performance, though the VAC-enabled multiplayer may be restricted to offline or LAN modes. The game's PC minimum GPU is roughly GTX 470 class, well below the Deck's RDNA 2 equivalent, so campaign and Zombies modes should run at 40–60 fps with tuned settings.
profiles.BasisNote: No Deck-specific player reports were found; profiles are estimated from the PC minimum requirements (GTX 470 minimum — well below the Deck's ~GTX 1050 Ti class GPU) and general Proton Gold compatibility. On first run, check frame rate during a busy Zombies round or gunfight-heavy campaign section, and drop to Optimal if you see sustained dips below your target.

MaxBattery.Notes: Render resolution dropped to 960×600 with FSR upscaling keeps GPU load minimal at 7 W TDP; motion blur and DoF disabled reduce GPU cost with no gameplay penalty. In-game option names are based on the standard Black Ops III PC settings menu, as no Deck-specific reports were available.

KnownIssues: VAC (Valve Anti-Cheat) may block online multiplayer matchmaking on Proton — offline campaign and Zombies are unaffected.
No Deck-specific player reports found; performance estimates are based on PC minimum requirements and Deck hardware class.
The game requires approximately 100 GB of storage, which may fill a base-model Deck's SSD.
Occasional shader compilation stutters on first launch or in new areas are expected under Proton.

MaxPerformance.Notes: The Deck's RDNA 2 GPU comfortably exceeds the game's minimum spec, so native 1280×800 with High textures is realistic; expect occasional dips to ~50 fps in dense Zombies hordes or crowded campaign setpieces. Battery life will be short at full TDP — keep a charger handy for extended sessions.

Optimal.Notes: A 40 Hz refresh rate with a matching frame cap delivers smooth, tear-free gameplay with a good visual balance. FSR upscaling from 1024x640 keeps the image sharp enough while giving the GPU headroom to hold the cap.

profiles.Summary: Call of Duty: Black Ops III is a 2015 first-person shooter that runs at Gold tier on Proton, meaning it generally works well but may require some configuration; the Steam Deck's RDNA 2 GPU comfortably exceeds the minimum PC requirements, so 60 fps at medium settings is achievable. No specific Deck player reports were found, so these profiles are estimated from PC requirements and hardware comparisons.
profiles.BasisNote: No Deck-specific reports were found; profiles are estimated from the PC minimum requirements (GTX 470 class minimum, well below the Deck's ~GTX 1050 Ti GPU) and general ProtonDB Gold tier behaviour. On your first run, check frame pacing in a high-action multiplayer or Zombies round and drop to the Optimal profile if the 60 fps cap proves unstable.

MaxBattery.Notes: Rendering at 960x600 with FSR upscaling and a locked 30 fps cap keeps TDP low for extended sessions. Disabling shadow-heavy and post-process effects has the biggest impact on battery life in this engine.

KnownIssues: VAC (Valve Anti-Cheat) is enabled, which may cause issues with online multiplayer under Proton — expect possible bans or connectivity problems in ranked/online modes.
The game requires ~100 GB of storage, which may be tight on base Steam Deck models.
Some users on ProtonDB report needing to set Proton to a specific version to avoid crashes on launch.
Split-screen and co-op modes may have reduced performance compared to solo play due to additional rendering overhead.

MaxPerformance.Notes: At native 1280x800 with high textures and TDP uncapped, the Deck can sustain 50-60 fps in most areas, though dense outdoor or high-action scenes may dip into the high 40s. Disable Motion Blur for cleaner visuals and slightly better framing.
